old: Never enter an unprotected trench 5 ft or deeper (4 ft or deeper in Washington, WAC 296-155-657), and don't assume shallow trenches are safe.
new: Never enter an unprotected trench 5 ft or deeper, and don't assume shallow trenches are safe; a state plan can set a shallower depth, so check the job's state.
why: national card: the one-state number (WA 4 ft, WAC 296-155-657) lives in sp-wa-trench-1, which is forced on WA trench questions

old: Of the 51 state tables in the app (50 states and DC, checked 2026-11-19): the wait is 2 working days in 28 states and 3 in 13, and longer in a few; ticket life runs from about two weeks to 60 days, counted in working days in some states and calendar days in others, and from the call in some and from the legal dig date in others; the tolerance zone is 18 inches each side in about as many states as 24 inches, measured from the mark in some and from the outside edge of the line in others.
new: No federal law sets the wait, the ticket life or the tolerance zone. The wait runs from 48 hours to 5 working days; ticket life runs from about two weeks to 60 days, counted in working days in some states and calendar days in others, and from the call in some and from the legal dig date in others; the tolerance zone is 18 or 24 inches each side in nearly every state, measured from the mark in some and from the outside edge of the line in others. The 811 by-state tables list each state's numbers.
why: the counts (28 / 13) came from the app table and differ from the by-state tables built from the cards; the tables now carry each state's group

old: The text of the excavation and confined space supplements was not read on 2026-11-20, so what they add is not confirmed: the federal 5 ft trench rule is the floor, and a crew should read the MOSH supplement or ask MOSH.
new: The excavation amendments keep the federal 5 ft trench rule and add that protective system records (tabulated data, designs) are kept at the jobsite (see Maryland's trench card); the confined space supplement's text was not read on 2026-11-20, so what it adds is not confirmed: ask MOSH.
why: contradicted sp-md-trench-1 (read later the same day), which has the Maryland amendments to 1926.652
